title: Korea Stock Market Today: Nov 10, 2026 - KOSPI Surges 4.39% to 5,239 as U.S. Chip Rally Sparks Rebound, NHN Hits Limit Up
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,239.13, up 4.39%, and KOSDAQ closed at 667.61, up 4.48%, as a sharp rally in U.S. chip stocks and dip buying after last week's plunge lifted both markets. Company-specific themes included NHN's strong third-quarter results, fuel cell stocks, a gas engine supply deal at HD Hyundai Construction Equipment, airlines, hair-loss drugs and Ukraine reconstruction.

IndexCloseChange
KOSPI5,239.13+4.39%

1. Sharp rebound — U.S. chip rally and dip buying

KOSPI opened at 5,247.22 (+4.55%) and rose as high as 5,300.92 (+5.62%) before closing at 5,239.13. KOSDAQ opened at 661.73 (+3.56%), reached 671.91 (+5.15%) and closed at 667.61.

Korean market coverage said the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped more than 6% overnight, with AMD and Broadcom among the strong names, and that lower oil prices and easing U.S. inflation worries improved global sentiment. Dip buying after last week's steep drop added to the move.

On KOSPI, foreign investors net bought about 353 billion won and institutions about 498 billion won, while individuals net sold about 1.34 trillion won (provisional). On KOSDAQ, foreigners net sold about 148 billion won and individuals about 56 billion won, while institutions net bought about 215 billion won.

2. Chips — large caps, PCB makers and equipment names

Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and Samsung Electro-Mechanics rebounded strongly, and buying spread to PCB, test and back-end equipment makers on expectations of higher demand from AI servers and high-performance chips.

3. NHN hits the upper limit — AI data center and cloud names

NHN hit the daily upper limit after reporting third-quarter operating profit of 58.8 billion won, up 112.6% from a year earlier, on sales of 758.3 billion won (up 21.2%) and net profit of 38.9 billion won. The company is also pursuing a 100 MW AI data center operation by 2027. Related infrastructure, power and construction names drew buying.

4. Fuel cells — Bloom Energy and data center power

As AI data centers strain power grids, interest grew in on-site power such as solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC). U.S. fuel cell maker Bloom Energy's role as a data center power option lifted its Korean supply chain. TNE Korea hit the upper limit.

5. Gas engines — HD Hyundai Construction Equipment

HD Hyundai Construction Equipment rose after reports of a roughly 160 billion won deal to supply gas power-generation engines to North American firm PSI, with 22-liter long blocks delivered over two years from 2027 for uses including AI data centers.

6. Airlines — Hanjin KAL stake fight and merger hopes

The stake contest between Hoban Group and Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae continued, and hopes that the Korean Air–Asiana integration will show effects from next year, including route expansion and cost savings, lifted airline stocks broadly.

7. Hair-loss drugs — baricitinib long-term data

Long-term follow-up of the phase 3 BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 trials reportedly showed about 85% of patients who responded at year one kept the response at year four. Baricitinib is a JAK inhibitor used for severe alopecia areata. Samik Pharmaceutical, which is developing a long-acting injectable using it, hit the upper limit.

8. Ukraine reconstruction — peace talks resume

Reports that U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks would resume in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11 lifted reconstruction and construction machinery names. Gaps on territory and ceasefire terms remain, so any real deal is uncertain.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 10?
KOSPI closed at 5,239.13 (+4.39%) and KOSDAQ at 667.61 (+4.48%). KOSPI touched 5,300.92 (+5.62%) intraday.

Why did Korean stocks rebound?
A reported 6%+ jump in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, easing oil and inflation worries, and dip buying after last week's plunge.

Why did NHN hit the upper limit?
Third-quarter operating profit rose 112.6% year on year to 58.8 billion won, and the company is pursuing a 100 MW AI data center operation by 2027.
